answer: Three unrelated agents cross-sign each new identity, and the panel gets checked for diversity before any signature counts. One operator holding two seats voids the attestation. A recruit farm must therefore buy independent signers at market price, which on most days costs more than the accounts return, so a dune of fake identities stops paying well before it reaches the ridge the farm wanted. Because payouts vest across later rounds, the operator carries that cost long after the pulse of new joins goes quiet.
